extracted.intended_audience: complainants, respondents, Ethics Commission staff, Commissioners, City employees, and attorneys involved in San Francisco Ethics Commission enforcement matters
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory rules and procedural standards governing filing, review, investigation, probable cause proceedings, hearings, penalties, and related administrative processes before the San Francisco Ethics Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: These regulations are intended to ensure the fair, just, and timely review, investigation, and hearing of complaints presented to the Commission by doing the following: Setting and maintaining objective standards for the investigation and prosecution of matters brought before the Commission; Eliminating any political or improper influence in the investigation and prosecution of persons accused of violations of laws within the Commission’s jurisdiction; Protecting the privacy rights of those accused of ethics violations by maintaining the confidentiality of complaints filed with, and investigations conducted by, the Commission; Providing a fair hearing for persons and entities accused of violations; Ensuring timely enforcement and complaint resolution; Coordinating and sharing with other governmental agencies the responsibility for investigations and prosecutions of complaints, whenever consistent with the interests of justice; and Delegating to the Commission staff maximum discretion in the handling and resolution of complaints at staff level, while retaining oversight of those staff activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement of objectives and guiding principles for all enforcement activity; establishes fairness, confidentiality, timeliness, interagency coordination, and staff delegation as governing standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement Authority (Scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: These regulations are applicable to potential violations of City laws relating to campaign finance, lobbying, campaign consulting, conflicts of interest, governmental ethics, the San Francisco Sunshine Ordinance, and the Whistleblower Protection Ordinance, as well as State laws relating to campaign finance, conflicts of interest, or governmental ethics, including, but not limited to: San Francisco Charter section 15.100 et seq. and Appendix C (Ethics); the San Francisco Campaign and Governmental Conduct Code; San Francisco Administrative Code, Chapter 67, et seq.; the Political Reform Act of 1974, Government Code section 81000 et seq.; Government Code section 1090 et seq.; and Government Code section 3201, et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the substantive legal provisions and subject-matter jurisdiction the regulations implement and enforce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of Key Terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides operative definitions for terms used in the regulations, including “City,” “Commission,” “Complainant,” “Enforcement action,” “Director of Enforcement,” “Deliver,” “Executive Director”/“Director,” “Probable cause,” “Respondent,” “Referral,” “Staff,” and “Violation of law.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies how terms are used throughout procedures (e.g., how delivery is effected, what constitutes probable cause), enabling consistent application of other rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sworn Complaint Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Sworn complaints must be made in writing on a form designated by the Executive Director or in a writing that contains all the information requested in the Director’s designated form. Sworn complaints must be signed by the complainant under penalty of perjury. Electronic signatures that conform with the Commission’s electronic signature policy sufficiently comply with this requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sworn complaints should include: the name and address of the respondent; the facts constituting an alleged violation(s) of law; the names and addresses of witnesses, if any; and copies of documents or other evidence that may be relevant to proving the fact(s) constituting the alleged violation(s). The Director of Enforcement must process and evaluate all sworn complaints pursuant to Preliminary Review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal Complaint Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal complaints may be submitted by telephone, in person, or in a writing. An informal complaint should include the name of the person or organization believed to have violated the law and the facts of the alleged violation. A complaint submitted on the prescribed complaint form that does not meet the requirements of a sworn complaint will be considered an informal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Enforcement Director has discretion to review informal complaints and should consider whether the information permits review and investigation; anonymous complaints are treated as informal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous Complaints Are Informal
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints may be submitted anonymously. Such complaints will be treated as informal complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymous status means the complaint will not be processed as a sworn complaint subject to mandatory processing; staff discretion governs whether to review/investigate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner Recusal for Commissioner-Initiated Complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member of the Commission who submits a formal or informal complaint must recuse him or herself from all consideration, review, investigation, or hearing of that complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents conflict of interest when a Commissioner is the complainant; ensures impartial handling by other Commissioners/staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sunshine Ordinance Complaint Handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to Section 67.34 of the San Francisco Administrative Code, the Commission will investigate complaints containing credible allegations against elected official(s) or department head(s) alleging willful violations of the Sunshine Ordinance. If a complaint filed with the Commission does not meet the criteria set forth in Section 67.34, the Commission will refer it to the Sunshine Ordinance Task Force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes public-document treatment and referral paths for Sunshine Ordinance allegations; specifies referral when statutory criteria unmet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of Complaint Does Not Bar Continued Investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may continue to investigate a complaint even if the complainant withdraws it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal by complainant does not automatically terminate Commission or staff enforcement activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Review by Director of Enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a sworn complaint, the Director of Enforcement will conduct a preliminary review of the complaint to determine whether there is reason to believe a violation of law may have occurred. This preliminary review may include reviewing documents, communicating with the complainant or respondent, and any other inquiry to determine whether a full investigation is warranted. If the Director of Enforcement determines there is reason to believe a violation of law has occurred, the Director of Enforcement will open an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the staff-level screening process and evidentiary threshold (reason to believe) to proceed to investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for Complaint Dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Director may dismiss the complaint if, based on the allegations and information contained in a complaint and the Director of Enforcement’s preliminary review, the Director of Enforcement determines that no violation of law has likely occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons for dismissal include but are not limited to: complaint lacks enough information for further investigation; credible evidence clearly refutes allegation; allegations, if true, do not constitute violation; complaint contains opinion rather than specific allegations; allegations already under investigation or resolved elsewhere; dismissal would better serve interest of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint Referral to Other Agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of Enforcement, with the concurrence of the Executive Director, may refer the matter to another government agency if the Director of Enforcement determines that the agency has jurisdiction and may more appropriately resolve the allegations in the complaint or enforce the applicable provisions of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral requires Executive Director concurrence; Commission notified pursuant to reporting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly Reporting of Dismissed Complaints to Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of Enforcement will provide a monthly summary to the Commission of each complaint dismissed including the reasons for dismissal provided. That summary will comply with the confidentiality requirements of the Charter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures Commission oversight of dismissal activity while respecting confidentiality constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whistleblower Retaliation Quarterly Reporting Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: No less than quarterly, the Director of Enforcement will provide a summary report to the Commission of the status of all complaints still under preliminary review that allege retaliation against whistleblowers. For matters that have been under preliminary review for more than 90 calendar days, the Director of Enforcement will provide an explanation for why the Commission’s staff has not completed its preliminary review as well as a target date for completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes monitoring and transparency obligations for whistleblower retaliation matters and timelines for long-pending prelim reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of Dismissal and Judicial Review
rubrics_metrics.description: A dismissal or closure of a complaint, after notification to the Commission pursuant to this Section, is a final decision and represents the end of the administrative process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a complainant desires further review, the complainant must follow procedures in Section 1094.5(a) of the California Code of Civil Procedure for judicial review of final administrative orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening an Investigation and Interagency Notice Timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after a preliminary review, the Director of Enforcement determines there is reason to believe a violation of law has occurred, the Director of Enforcement will open an investigation. Upon opening an investigation, the Director of Enforcement will immediately forward the complaint to the District Attorney and City Attorney. Within 10 business days after receipt of the complaint, the District Attorney and City Attorney will inform the Director of Enforcement in writing regarding whether they have initiated or intend to pursue an investigation of the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If neither DA nor City Attorney pursues the matter, the Director of Enforcement has 14 calendar days after receiving that notification to notify the complainant of action/inaction and reasons; if no decision within 14 days the complainant will be notified of the delay and later updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Ex Parte Communications During Investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an investigation is opened and until the Commission has made a final decision or order, whether by stipulation or otherwise, members of the Commission will not engage in oral or written communications with the parties or any member of the public outside of a Commission meeting, witness interview or examination, or settlement conference regarding the merits of an enforcement action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects impartiality of Commissioners and preserves integrity of adjudicative process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpoena and Subpoena Duces Tecum Issuance Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Director may issue subpoenas and subpoenas duces tecum on behalf of the Commission. A subpoena or subpoena duces tecum may not be issued unless the Executive Director finds that the person to be subpoenaed or the information to be requested in the subpoena duces tecum is relevant to a specific matter under investigation or that the person or entity to be subpoenaed controls relevant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits subpoena issuance to relevancy and control of information; provides staff authority to compel evidence where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and Service Timing for Subpoenas
rubrics_metrics.description: If a subpoena duces tecum seeks production of personal or financial records, the Enforcement Director will provide notice as required by California Government Code section 7460, et seq. Subpoenas will be served at least 15 calendar days before the time required for attendance. Subpoenas duces tecum will be served at least 25 calendar days before the time required for attendance or production of the requested documents. Service must be made as set forth in Section 2(F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies minimum advance service periods to allow compliance or objections, with special notice rules for sensitive records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance Mechanisms for Subpoenas
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director of Enforcement consents, any person subject to a subpoena duces tecum may satisfy it by delivering the requested documents together with an affidavit in compliance with Section 1561 of the California Evidence Code. If a person or entity refuses to comply with a subpoena or subpoena duces tecum, the Executive Director may ask the City Attorney to petition the San Francisco Superior Court for an order compelling compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides alternative compliance method and judicial enforcement path for refusals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection Process for Subpoenas
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person or entity served with a subpoena or subpoena duces tecum may object by filing written objections with the Executive Director at least 5 calendar days before the time required for attendance or production. The Executive Director will rule on objections and issue a written order at least one calendar day before the time required for attendance or production. The Executive Director’s decision is final. Failure to file timely objections waives all grounds for any objection. Any motion to quash or modify in Superior Court must inform the Executive Director in writing on the same day the motion is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates tight timelines for objections and makes Exec Director ruling final absent immediate court action; emphasizes notice of court motions to Exec Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of Investigations and Sanctions for Unauthorized Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations will be conducted in a confidential manner. Records of any investigation will be considered confidential information to the extent permitted by state law. All investigative documents, including notes and memoranda, created prior to the probable cause determination, such as the complaint, will remain confidential. All investigative documents created by the Executive Director and staff after the probable cause determination shall be confidential, unless and until introduced as evidence or as an exhibit for a hearing on the merits. Any member or employee who, prior to a determination concerning probable cause, discloses information about any preliminary investigation, except as necessary to conduct the investigation, will be subject to an administrative enforcement action and may be deemed guilty of official misconduct. The unauthorized release of confidential information will be sufficient grounds for termination or removal of the commissioner responsible for such release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict confidentiality regime intended to protect privacy and integrity of preliminary investigations, with serious employment/disciplinary consequences for breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page Limitations and Format Requirements for Filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Probable Cause Report and Hearing Brief will be limited to 25 pages, exclusive of attachments. Responses to the Probable Cause Report and Hearing Brief will be limited to 25 pages; any rebuttal or reply limited to 10 pages; all other filings limited to 10 pages, exclusive of attachments. A “page” means one side of an 8½ x 11-inch page, with margins of at least one inch, typewritten and double-spaced in no smaller than twelve-point type. Each page and attachments will be consecutively numbered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforces brevity and uniform formatting for filings; attachments excluded from page counts; defines page format precisely for compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probable Cause Closure for Interest of Justice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of Enforcement may recommend closure of a complaint if it falls within the Commission’s jurisdiction, but closure rather than initiating probable cause proceedings would better serve the interest of justice. Causes include de minimis violations; further prosecution would not further the law's purpose; the law was struck down; respondent came into full compliance prior to initiating an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits discretion to close matters where enforcement is unnecessary or counterproductive, subject to Executive Director concurrence and Commission notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation and Limits for Probable Cause Hearing Officer Duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission delegates responsibility for conducting Probable Cause Conferences to the Executive Director, but the Commission retains authority to make probable cause findings. The Executive Director may not recommend a probable cause determination unless the respondent(s) has been provided an opportunity to respond to a Probable Cause Report and appear in person to make oral argument, if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation accelerates staff handling while preserving Commission's final authority; procedural fairness guaranteed by opportunity to respond and appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Contents of the Probable Cause Report
rubrics_metrics.description: The Probable Cause Report must include: identification of the alleged violations; a summary of the laws at issue; a statement of the evidence gathered through the investigation, including any exculpatory and mitigating information; notification that the respondent has the right to respond in writing to the Probable Cause Report; notification that the respondent has the right to request a Probable Cause Conference and be present and represented; and any other relevant material or argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures respondents receive full statement of allegations, legal basis, and evidence including exculpatory matters; triggers response and conference rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whistleblower Complainant Participation Rights in Probable Cause Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Complainants who have alleged retaliation pursuant to Section 4.115 may participate in probable cause proceedings. Participation may include providing additional evidence to the Executive Director or writing an independent response to the Probable Cause Report. Complainants must deliver a request to participate in writing within 10 calendar days of issuance of the Probable Cause Report. The Executive Director shall have discretion to define scope of participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives whistleblower complainants limited participation rights subject to Exec Director's scope control; requires timely request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response Deadline to Probable Cause Report
rubrics_metrics.description: Each respondent may submit a written Response to the Probable Cause Report, containing evidence, legal arguments, and mitigating or exculpatory information. Responses must be delivered to the Executive Director and all other respondents not later than 21 calendar days following service of the Probable Cause Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a fixed 21-calendar-day response period and content expectations for respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director of Enforcement Rebuttal Deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of Enforcement may submit evidence or argument in rebuttal to the response. When the Director of Enforcement submits a rebuttal, the Director must deliver a copy to all respondents not later than 14 calendar days following the date the response was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows staff to reply and close written exchange with a defined rebuttal timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible Evidence at Probable Cause Stage
rubrics_metrics.description: The evidence recited in the Probable Cause Report, Response, and Rebuttal may rely on witness declarations, hearsay evidence (including declarations of investigators or others relating the statements of witnesses or concerning the examination of physical evidence), and any other relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopts relaxed evidence standards at probable cause stage, permitting hearsay and investigator declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for Extension of Time Pre-Probable Cause
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Director may extend time limitations in this Section for good cause. At any time prior to a determination of probable cause, the Executive Director may allow submission of additional material. Parties seeking extensions must file a request with the Executive Director in writing at least 5 calendar days prior to the original deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits flexible scheduling for fairness; requires timely written extension requests showing good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probable Cause Conference Confidentiality and Request Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Probable cause conferences shall be confidential and closed to the public unless the respondent requests and all other respondents agree that it be open. The Executive Director, Director of Enforcement, or any respondent(s) may request a Probable Cause Conference by serving the request no later than 21 calendar days after delivery of the Probable Cause Report unless the Executive Director extends the time for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality preserves preliminary process; respondents have right to request conference within 21 days; Exec Director may set conference time and permit additional materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probable Cause Conference Procedures: Representation and Witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: The Probable Cause Conference is informal. The respondent may bring legal counsel or other representative. The Executive Director may allow witnesses to attend and participate; a party requesting witness testimony must deliver a written request to the Executive Director and all parties within 7 calendar days of the conference. The Executive Director will consider relevance, witness interest, and fairness in allowing testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives parties representation rights and structured process for witness participation requests with short deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and Transcript Rights for Probable Cause Conference
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Probable Cause Conference will be audio recorded. The Director of Enforcement will retain the recording until the opportunity for legal challenge has been exhausted. The audio recording will be provided to the respondent upon request. A respondent may ask that a certified court reporter attend at the respondent’s cost; that respondent will provide copies of the transcript to the Executive Director and all other respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves an official record; respondents may incur cost for court reporter but must share transcript copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translator Request for Probable Cause Conference
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may request the presence of a City-approved translator for the Probable Cause Conference. The request must be made in writing at least 20 calendar days before the conference and copies delivered to all parties. The requesting party shall bear the cost of translation services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures language access but places translation cost on requesting party and requires 20-day lead time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Director’s Recommended Probable Cause Standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Director may recommend a finding of probable cause to believe a violation has occurred if the evidence is sufficient to lead a person of ordinary caution and prudence to believe or entertain a strong suspicion that a respondent committed or caused a violation. A recommended finding does not constitute a finding that a violation has occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the threshold for staff recommendation as a strong suspicion standard (person of ordinary caution/prudence); distinguishes recommendation from final adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for a Written Recommended Finding of Probable Cause
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Executive Director recommends a finding of probable cause, the finding must be in writing and must be based solely on the evidence and argument presented in the Probable Cause Report, Response, and Rebuttal, as well as any evidence or argument presented at the Probable Cause Conference. The recommended finding must contain a summary of all evidence and arguments presented at the conference, and the Executive Director’s assessment of that evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires written documentation tying recommendation to record and explaining staff assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding of No Probable Cause Must Be Written with Reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Executive Director determines that probable cause does not exist, the Executive Director will issue a finding of no probable cause in writing. The finding will provide clear and concise reasons supporting that determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates reasoned written dispositions for denials of probable cause to support finality and potential review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default Orders for Failure to Appear at Probable Cause Conference
rubrics_metrics.description: If proper notice procedures were followed and the respondent(s) failed to appear for the Probable Cause Conference, the Executive Director may make a recommendation for a finding of probable cause adverse to the interests of the non-appearing respondent(s). The Director of Enforcement bears the burden of proving that respondent(s) were properly served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows adverse recommendation on default when service established; places burden on staff to prove notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframe for Probable Cause Determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Director will make a probable cause determination within 60 calendar days after the later of the date the Probable Cause Report was served, the date the Probable Cause Conference was held, or the date the last pleading was received if no conference is held. The Executive Director will not make a determination before the respondent’s deadline to respond. The Executive Director will deliver the determination to each respondent and the Director of Enforcement within 7 calendar days of making the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes a 60-day target for staff determinations and prompt delivery of determinations within 7 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission Review and Ratification of Exec Director Probable Cause Determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon finalizing a recommended probable cause determination the Executive Director will inform the Commission by the next business day. Any member of the Commission may request review of the recommendation in closed session at the next regularly scheduled meeting, provided the request is received within 5 calendar days of notification. If any Commissioner requests review, the determination is not final until at least three members ratify it at the next meeting. If no request for review, Commission ratifies by inaction and the Executive Director will publish the formal Probable Cause Determination to parties and post it to the website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives Commissioners short window (5 days) to call up matters; requires a 3-member ratification if called up; establishes publishing procedure when ratified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of Findings of No Probable Cause
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission’s finding of no probable cause is a final decision and represents the end of the administrative process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complainants seeking further review must pursue judicial review under CCP 1094.5(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Prior Formal Written Advice as a Defense
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Director will not make a finding of probable cause if presented with clear and convincing evidence that, prior to the alleged violation: the respondent had requested and obtained written formal advice from the Commission; the respondent disclosed truthfully all facts pertinent; the Commission or its staff issued a written opinion with which both the District Attorney and City Attorney concurred; and the respondent committed the acts in good-faith reliance upon the written opinion of the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes good-faith reliance on authoritative Commission advice as a complete shield against probable cause where rigorous conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation to a Hearing Officer for Pre-Hearing and Hearing Duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon majority approval, the Commission may delegate authority to preside over a hearing on the merits to a hearing officer. Any licensed California attorney or individual member of the Commission may serve as a hearing officer. When an individual Commissioner or hearing officer is assigned to hear and decide preliminary matters, he or she will make an actual determination. Procedural determinations may be reviewed by the Commission upon request by the Executive Director or a respondent. After presiding over a hearing on the merits, the hearing officer must submit a report and recommendation to the Commission containing proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law. Copies must be delivered no later than 30 calendar days after the hearing concludes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides flexibility to use hearing officers while preserving Commission oversight and sets timelines for issuance of reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling and Notice of Hearing on the Merits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Director will schedule the hearing on the merits and deliver written notice of the date, time, and location at least 30 calendar days prior to the commencement of the hearing. The notice must include specified language advising respondents of rights to be present, to be represented, to present evidence, to cross-examine witnesses, and to request subpoenas on or before a specified date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires 30-day notice with a standardized form of notice that identifies procedural rights and subpoena request deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission as Hearing Panel Default
rubrics_metrics.description: Following issuance of a Finding of Probable Cause, the Commission will proceed with a hearing on the merits. Unless otherwise decided by the Commission, the Commission will sit as the hearing panel to hear the merits of the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default adjudicatory body is the full Commission unless delegation occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery Entitlement Pre-Hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Director and each respondent will be entitled to pre-hearing discovery in accordance with the California Administrative Procedure Act, Government Code, Title 2, Division 3, Part 1, Chapter 5, section 11500 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery follows CA APA rules; parties have rights to obtain evidence pre-hearing as provided by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpoena Requests for Hearing on the Merits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Director and any respondent named in the Finding of Probable Cause may request issuance of subpoenas to compel witnesses and production of documents at the hearing on the merits. Requests should be delivered no later than 20 calendar days prior to the hearing and must be accompanied by a declaration specifying names/addresses and materiality of testimony or a specific description of documents sought and why necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets 20-day pre-hearing deadline and declaration content requirements for subpoena requests; subpoenas issued upon approval of Commission or hearing officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing Briefs: Content, Page Limits, and Deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Director will, and any respondent may, submit a hearing brief outlining significant legal arguments and listing evidence and witnesses; may attach anticipated evidence. Unless Commission or hearing officer agrees to accept email, six copies of Staff’s Hearing Brief must be delivered no later than 30 calendar days prior to hearing. Respondent’s responsive brief due no later than 15 calendar days prior; Staff’s rebuttal due no later than 5 calendar days prior. See Section 6 for page and format limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies content expectations, strict copy and deadline rules for pre-hearing briefs to support orderly hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Matters: Motion Timing and Topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may request formal consideration of preliminary matters by delivering a motion setting forth facts, law, and argument. Preliminary matters may include procedural matters, disqualification of Commission members, requests for dismissal of charges as a matter of law, discovery motions, and any other matters not related to truth/falsity of factual allegations. Requests must be delivered no later than 15 calendar days prior to hearing; responses due 10 days prior; replies due 7 days prior. Copies must be delivered to Executive Director and every other respondent when filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an accelerated schedule and delivery requirements for resolving preliminary procedural or legal threshold issues before hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording of Hearings on the Merits
rubrics_metrics.description: Every hearing on the merits will be recorded digitally. The Commission will retain the tapes until the opportunity for legal challenge has been exhausted. Copies of a tape will be available upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures an official record of hearings for appellate review or other purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place of Delivery and Authorized Addresses for Service
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever regulations require delivery to the Commission, its members, or the Executive Director, delivery will be made at Staff’s office. Delivery to a respondent or committee will be effective if made by first-class U.S. mail, personal delivery, or any other means agreed upon. The Commission may rely on addresses listed with Controller/Payroll for City employees, retirement system for former employees, the address provided to the Ethics Commission for registered candidates/committees, or an address reasonably calculated to give notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes default delivery locations and prioritizes official addresses maintained by City departments or by the Ethics Commission for effective service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary Dismissal Procedure by Executive Director
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time after the Probable Cause Determination, the Executive Director may request voluntary dismissal of all or part of an enforcement action for good cause by filing a Request for Voluntary Dismissal with the Commission. The Commission must consider the request in closed session at its next meeting. If ratified, Commission will take no further action; if denied, Commission may provide guidance on additional information desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides mechanism to resolve matters administratively with Commission oversight; dismissal requires Commission ratification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of Proof at Hearing on the Merits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may determine that a respondent has committed a violation of law only if a person of ordinary caution and prudence would conclude, based on a preponderance of the evidence, that the respondent has committed or caused the violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopts preponderance of the evidence standard for final adjudication (more likely than not).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of Evidence and Parties’ Rights at Hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: All evidence admissible in an administrative proceeding governed by the California Administrative Procedure Act will be admissible. The Executive Director and each respondent have the right to call and examine witnesses under oath, introduce exhibits, cross-examine and impeach witnesses, and rebut evidence presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing evidentiary regime follows CA APA; parties have full procedural rights to present and challenge evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translator Request for Hearing on the Merits
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may request a City-approved translator in writing at least 20 calendar days before the hearing and must deliver a copy to all parties simultaneously. The requesting party bears the cost of translation services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures language access for hearings, with cost and lead-time requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibits Admissibility and Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where both parties stipulate to admissibility of an exhibit, parties must advise Commission in advance. For other exhibits, each party must move to admit at the hearing and the other party may object prior to ruling. The briefs may attach anticipated evidence but are not required to list rebuttal evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages stipulation to streamline hearings; formal admission occurs at hearing with opportunity to object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness Examination Order and Commissioner Questioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Witnesses will be examined by the parties as follows: direct examination, cross-examination, re-direct. After parties conclude their examination, Commissioners will have an opportunity to pose questions to the witness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies examination sequence and gives Commissioners post-examination questioning rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties and Remedies the Commission May Impose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may impose administrative penalties in amounts authorized by law; where the law does not specify amounts, the Commission may impose penalties up to $5,000 for each violation, or three times the amount improperly unreported or unlawfully contributed/expended/received, whichever is greater. The Commission may order forfeiture of campaign contributions that do not comply with the Campaign Finance Reform Ordinance and any other relief deemed appropriate and within its authority under Charter section C3.699-13. Unless otherwise ordered, penalties must be paid in full within 90 calendar days of the Commission’s decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates monetary and equitable remedies including treble damages or statutory maxima; sets 90-day payment default timeline unless otherwise ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty Factors to Consider in Assessing Orders
rubrics_metrics.description: When deciding on an order and penalties, the Commission will consider all relevant circumstances including but not limited to: the severity of the violation; presence or absence of intention to conceal, deceive, or mislead; whether violation was willful; whether isolated or part of pattern; prior record of violations; degree of cooperation and willingness to remedy; and the respondent’s ability to pay (mitigating if documented with three years’ tax returns and six months’ bank records or accounting statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides multi-factor mitigation/aggravation framework and documentation requirements for inability-to-pay claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding of No Violation Finality and Announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission determines insufficient evidence to establish a violation, the Commission will publicly announce this fact. No further action will be taken. Complainants seeking further review must pursue CCP 1094.5(a) judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public announcement and administrative finality for findings of no violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default Orders for Failure to Appear at Hearing on the Merits
rubrics_metrics.description: If proper notice was followed and respondent(s) failed to appear before the Commission for a hearing, the Commission may enter an order adverse to the non-appearing respondent(s), including Default Orders for injunctive relief and administrative penalties after a hearing on the merits. The Executive Director bears burden of proving proper service. A default order is a final administrative order subject to judicial review under CCP 1094.5(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows final default adjudications when service and notice are shown; default orders are final for appeal purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of Sunshine Ordinance Referrals: Public Document and Show Cause Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints alleging willful violations of the Sunshine Ordinance by elected officials and department heads are public documents pursuant to section 67.35. If a City officer or employee fails to comply with an Order of Determination by the Sunshine Ordinance Task Force or Supervisor of Records, they may refer the matter to the Ethics Commission for enforcement. After receipt, the Commission will schedule a Show Cause Hearing at the next regularly scheduled meeting provided parties are given at least 15 calendar days’ notice. The Show Cause Hearing will be open to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sunshine referrals involve public proceedings, a shorter 15-day notice for Show Cause hearings, and distinct evidentiary/review approaches described below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of Proof and Standard of Review for Sunshine Referrals
rubrics_metrics.description: For Sunshine Ordinance referrals, the respondent(s) will have the burden to prove they did not commit a violation as documented by the SOTF’s Order of Determination and referral. Where appropriate, the Commission will defer to findings of fact set forth in the SOTF’s Order; conclusions of law will be reviewed independently (de novo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives deference to fact findings from referring body but subjects legal conclusions to independent review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show Cause Hearing Procedures and Time Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: At a Show Cause Hearing, complainant and respondent each have 10 minutes to present argument and may reserve up to 3 minutes for rebuttal. Witnesses may speak for 3 minutes. The Commission, through the Chair, may extend testimony. The referring agency representative may present for 5 minutes before the hearing and is not a party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets strict time limits for oral presentations at Show Cause hearings and allows limited participation by the referring agency as a third-party friend of the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary Standards for Sunshine Referrals
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal rules of evidence do not apply to hearings on referrals to enforce orders of the Sunshine Ordinance. If any party presents evidence at the Show Cause Hearing that was not presented to the SOTF, the Commission may remand the referral to the SOTF for further deliberation and review of the new evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopts flexible evidentiary approach but preserves option to remand for additional fact-finding if new evidence emerges at the Commission level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available Remedies for Sunshine Ordinance Violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon finding a violation of the Sunshine Ordinance, the Commission may impose any remedies set forth in Charter section C3-699.13, except the Commission may not impose administrative penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies limited by charter; administrative penalties excluded for Sunshine referrals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willful Misconduct Finding and Referral to Appointing Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission determines that an elected official, department head, or managerial city employee willfully failed to discharge duties imposed by the Sunshine Ordinance, Brown Act, or Public Records Act, the Commission may find that the official committed official misconduct and, if the employee/official is identified in Section 15.105 of the Charter, must refer the finding to the official’s appointing authority as required by Charter Section 15.105.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates pathway to potential personnel or appointing-authority consequences for willful misconduct findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekend and Holiday Filing Deadline Rule for Late Filing Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as identified, filings due on a Saturday, Sunday, or City-recognized holiday but filed no later than the next business day will not be assessed late filing fees. The Ethics Commission’s electronic filing system will recognize the next business day as the filing deadline where applicable. Late filing fees will not be waived for Late Contribution Reports (Form 497) or Late Independent Expenditure Reports (496) due the weekend before an election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides deference for weekend/holiday deadlines with specific exception for certain pre-election reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic and Paper Filing Deadline Times
rubrics_metrics.description: All electronic filings must be submitted to the Commission’s electronic filing system by 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time on the deadline. All paper filings must be received in paper format or by facsimile by 5:00 p.m. on the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies exact cutoff times for different filing mediums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver Request Process for Late Filing Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons owing late filing fees may request reduction or waiver by responding to the Executive Director’s initial notice in writing. The request must explain why filing was non-willful, why enforcement would not further the law, identify good cause, provide adequate documentation demonstrating facts underlying the request, and be signed by the responsible party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver requests must be timely (see deadline below) and substantively supported with documentary proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for Waiver Requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The waiver request must be received by the Commission within 14 calendar days of the date on the Commission’s initial non-specific written notice. The Commission will presumptively deny requests received past this deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes strict 14-day filing window for waiver requests to avoid presumptive denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good Cause Categories for Waiver of Late Filing Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The following factors will presumptively qualify as 'good cause' and are grounds for a waiver: incapacitation for medical reasons (documentation: signed statement by board-certified physician/psychologist/psychotherapist/chiropractor on letterhead identifying filer, nature and dates); death (documentation: death certificate, published notice, or obituary); act of God (documentation: police/fire/insurance report indicating date and extent); other unique reasons beyond filer’s control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines acceptable documentary evidence and categories of good cause that generally justify waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Good-Cause Examples for Waiver Requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The following do not constitute 'good cause' and are not grounds for a waiver: first-time filer, not receiving notice of filing requirements, not being available to sign forms, not sending filing to proper official, not knowing where to get forms, not having complete information by deadline, not picking up mail, secretarial error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists common excuses that will not justify waiver to promote compliance and certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lobbyist-Related Waiver Notice Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to Section 2.145, the Executive Director must notify members of the Commission if the reduction or waiver of a late filing fee equals or exceeds $500 and the fee resulted from a late filed lobbyist disclosure. The Executive Director will follow Section 2.145 requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adds transparency and higher-level notice for significant lobbyist-related fee waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion to Enforcement Action for Large Late Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Director reserves the right to convert matters involving candidates and committees with late-filed reports that have generated more than $2,000 in late filing fees to enforcement actions handled pursuant to these Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threshold-driven escalation to formal enforcement for large accruals of late fees to ensure accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipulated Orders and Settlement Conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time, the Executive Director may enter negotiations to resolve allegations by way of a stipulated order. The stipulated order will set forth pertinent facts and may include agreements as to anything the Commission could order under Charter section C3.699-13. The stipulated order must explicitly state: it is subject to Commission approval; the respondent knowingly and voluntarily waives all procedural rights; the respondent acknowledges the stipulation is not binding on other law enforcement agencies; the stipulation becomes null and void if Commission refuses to approve it; and in the event of rejection and a full hearing, no member of the Commission will be disqualified because of prior consideration of the stipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows settlements with detailed waivers and conditions, but preserves other agencies’ authority and Commission’s final approval role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Admissibility of Unsuccessful Settlement Negotiations
rubrics_metrics.description: The details and supporting documentation for unsuccessful settlement negotiations are non-admissible in subsequent administrative enforcement actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects settlement negotiations from use as evidence to encourage candid settlement discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installment Plans for Payment of Assessed Penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: As a rule, the Executive Director will not accept offers to pay assessed administrative penalties in installments without proof of inability to pay as set forth in Section 9(E). Upon proof of inability to pay, the Executive Director may consider installment offers, but installment agreements must require full payment before expiration of 6 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits limited installment arrangements only with documented inability-to-pay and short maximum payment period (6 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing Administrative Penalties in Settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing administrative penalties for settlement negotiation, Staff will follow the rules set forth in Section 9(E) of these regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires penalty calculations and mitigation/aggravation to follow consistent guidelines enumerated in Section 9(E) (Penalty Factors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent Calendar and Commission Review of Stipulated Orders
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Executive Director enters a stipulated order, the Executive Director will inform the Commission. Any member may request the stipulated order be reviewed in public session by the full panel at the next meeting; requests must be received by 12:00 p.m. on the fifth calendar day prior to the meeting. If no member requests review, the stipulated order will be placed on the public agenda under 'Consent Calendar.' Members of the public may comment on any stipulated order on the Consent Calendar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates transparent opportunity for Commissioners to pull matters for public consideration and for public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission Approval Required for Stipulated Orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Stipulated orders must be approved by the Commission and, upon approval, must be announced publicly. The stipulated order will have the full force of a final order of the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalizes settlements only through Commission action; approved stipulations carry same weight as final orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retaliation Notification for Stipulated Orders Finding Retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 days of the Commission’s execution of a stipulated order finding that a respondent(s) has retaliated against a City employee in violation of Section 4.115, the Executive Director will notify the Clerk of the Board of Supervisors by sending a copy of the Commission’s final order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates prompt inter-branch notification when stipulated orders involve retaliation findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commencement of Administrative Enforcement Action Defined for Statute of Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise stated in City or State law, an action or proceeding for administrative penalties is brought or commenced by the Executive Director on the date the Director of Enforcement delivers the Probable Cause Report. If there is no statute of limitations for violations, the Probable Cause Report must be delivered within four years of the date of the alleged violation of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines triggering event for statute-of-limitations and establishes four-year outer limit when no specific statute exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolling the Statute of Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The four-year limitations period is tolled if the respondent(s) engaged in concealment or deceit for the period of concealment, or if the respondent(s) fails to comply with a subpoena or subpoena duces tecum from the date compliance was originally required until the date compliance is achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates equitable tolling for concealment/deceit and for periods of noncompliance with compulsory process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability Clause
rubrics_metrics.description: If any provision of these Regulations, or the application thereof to any person or circumstance, is held invalid, the validity of the remainder of the Regulations and the applicability of such provisions to other persons and circumstances will not be affected thereby.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard severability provision preserving remaining regulations when a provision is invalidated.
